title: Decoder floors are tight in the frontier format: one F2^9 label table, factors in col M of a rank-8 realisation (P112 64, E8 72, P104 (#968's unit) 56; two-call batches 128) — no κ claim
body:
## Decoder floors are tight in the frontier format: one F2^9 label table, factors in col M of a rank-8 realisation (P112 64, E8 72, P104 (#968's unit) 56; two-call batches 128) — no κ claim

**Status: research note, no κ claim** (scoped negative result with explicit open items). The selected frontier is unchanged. **Draft: overnight closures from the author's working cards are added below as RECORDED (not re-run by `verify.sh`); to be reviewed before marking ready.**

## Summary

This package pins down where the E8-family decoder (the copy cost of the P112 / E8 / P104 / E7 units, and of independent batches of them) can still be improved. In the format the frontier actually uses — **one global `F2^9` label table** (the pairing of the whole unit has `F2`-rank `≤ 9`; `≤ 7` for E7), **factors in the column space of a rank-8 (minimal-rank) realisation** (the square decoder of a rank-9 realisation is OPEN), any number of terms, any number of independent calls — the floors are **P112 64, E8 72, P104 56 (P104 = #968's unit, `F1 = H4`; other P104 units are not claimed), E7 49, and 64k for `k` independent P112 calls (128 for two; symmetric / physical table for `k ≥ 3`, `GL` charts with `k ≥ 3` are open)**, all attained. Every escape from that class is listed as OPEN with what it would have to achieve. Nothing here is a word-side result, and no κ is claimed.

## Results (labels: PROVEN / CHECKED / RECORDED / OPEN; full proofs and the master table are in the README)

1. **Theorem R, rigidity of the minimal-rank label table (CHECKED, 16 DRAT-verified UNSAT).** On E8, P112, P104 (#968's unit, `F1 = H4`, which lies in the 759 class, and one frame from each of the three invariant classes of disjoint second frames: three classes, four instances), the bit unit P111 (rank `≤ 9`, general `UVᵀ` and symmetric `PPᵀ`) and on E7, E6 (rank `≤ 7`), every fitting pairing of that rank is the dense pairing. **Credit: the P111 row is prior work.** #620 (GamingPuzzled) found by SAT that the rank-9 fitting matrix of its archived P111 pattern is unique, and #1097 (bitplane, merged) proof-checked it with LRAT in the general (asymmetric) model; #1097's set is the archived Hamming order with 9 indices deleted, which is not #589's set (104 of 111 lines in common), so Theorem R re-derives it on #589's puncture in both models with DRAT. #1815 (jmbarrancoml, merged) proved a one-sided P112 fitting rigidity (fixed column spaces); Theorem R removes that hypothesis. New here: E8, P112, P104, E7, E6. Controls (10, SAT, dense) and negative controls (sub-units at `h = 9`; P112 at `h = 10`, SAT and non-dense) are replayed. So at `h = 9` the "any `B`" slack of overcomplete decoders does not exist; non-dense tables start at `h ≥ 10`.
2. **Theorem P (PROVEN from a CHECKED census): P112 ≥ 64 in every rank-8 realisation** with factors in `col M` (every square decoder, any `m` otherwise) — #2277 had P112 ≥ 56 here and listed 64 as open. A support-propagation lemma certifies every label class except exactly the 8 (P112) / 16 (P104, #968's unit; the census was run on this unit only) Gram-deficient ones, which contain no 2-dimensional subspace and pair at rank 8 (P112) / ≥ 7 (P104). E8 72, E7 49, P104 (#968's) 56 follow (also #2277 Cor. 5.3). Attained by the decoders recomputed in `c5`.
3. **≤ 8 paid terms with factors anywhere ⇒ ≥ 64 (PROVEN)**; **#1180's nine-term example outside `col M` costs exactly 65 and its shape costs ≥ 64 for every admissible `B`** (it is a split of a proportional pair; CHECKED); all 120 co-star dead sets span in every rank-8 realisation, so every nine-term masked co-star decoder (Discussion 1267) is a square decoder of a rank-9 realisation (CHECKED + PROVEN consequence).
4. **Batching (PROVEN from CHECKED premises).** `k = 2` independent P112 calls on one `F2^9` table cost `≥ 128 + 3t` for every chart (`O(9)` and `GL(9)`), any rank-8 realisations, any `m`; `k ≥ 3` (symmetric / physical table; `GL` charts with `k ≥ 3` are open) `≥ 64k + 3t`. Some `O(9)` charts make all 64 cross pairs rank 7, so the counting bound 120 is not the truth: the extra units come from a rank argument. **#2294 (thakrarsagar) proves the `k = 2` / `O(9)` / Gram core first** and is credited; ours was derived independently, with `GL(9)`, general rank-8 realisations and `k ≥ 3` as additions.
5. **Every admissible `B` on one coordinate block (CHECKED, 8 DRAT):** `rank_F2 B[N(f), N(f)] ≥ 8`; and clique-hitting bounds on punctures (`f(2) ≥ 14`, `f(6) ≥ 46`, `f(7) ≥ 52`), with `s/f(s) ≤ 1/7` on all computed values (`s = 2..8`; `s = 3–5` RECORDED, `s = 1` not computed).
6. **RECORDED, not re-run here (the author's working cards; scopes quoted, labels not upgraded):**
   - **Bit windows of 13–14 totals: CLOSED (RECORDED).** Word-priced P111 set-decoders with ≤ 14 totals cost ≥ 63 (`STRAYS-BIT`: `n ≤ 13` PROVEN by exact rational Farkas certificates; `n = 14` CHECKED, 735 integer-only classes kissat UNSAT + drat-trim VERIFIED); P110 with ≤ 12 totals ≥ 63 (its whole hosting window); the premise (P) is proven and no longer used; P111 / P110 rigidity at `h = 9` drat-trim VERIFIED in the card (P111 rigidity credit: #620, #1097). `n ≥ 15` is hosting-forbidden (`R ≤ 4v`), a note.
   - **Projected-copy route to P110 = 62 (RECORDED pricing, not a theorem).** SPEC-legal (a checker convention forbids it, not the SPEC; `SPECCHECK`), but on PR589's tuned chains the best term costs ≥ 3.57% c net including the +2.80% unit gain (`BITCUT`); ideal bound +0.27% c is not attainable with those chains. Not a supplier.
   - **`h = 10` root code (Gram realisation): CLOSED (RECORDED; card status CHECKED).** Any `m`, any fitting `B` of rank ≤ 10: every term ≥ 8, P112 ≥ 64 (`STRAYS-H10`; 46/46 `G`-query DRATs verified, 688 term queries UNSAT with **DRATs pending (1 verified; README rows 16a/19a)**).
   - **`p = 45` closed for `m ≥ 8` (RECORDED; card: PROVEN from CHECKED exact data)**: cost ≥ 40 > 39.71 (Theorem 45, dense `B`, column-space factors); Lemma G (PROVEN) for `rank N = 8` (`PUNCT4`, `PUNCT5`).
   - Also recorded: E8 square root-code decoders ≥ 72 for every `B` (4022 pair classes, DRAT in the working card); `D4 ≥ 12` for every decoder; E7 square maximal-normal ≥ 49 for every `B`; no helper-free nested delivery of #968's P104 decoder for any `F2^9` table; PUNCT2 `p = 25..44` for any physical table. None of rows 1–5 depends on any of this.
7. **New tool (PROVEN, proof in README §3.3): the frame-module theorem.** For every nine-term decoder of a unit with 8-frames (any realisation, any rank, factors anywhere) the frame cross matrix is `J = I − νπᵀ/(π·ν)` with `π·ν ≠ 0`, `p(e) = Σ_f (M_ef/M_ff) p(f) + λ_e π`, and the Schur defect is rank one; it is a realisation-free rank-9 Lemma 1.1 as a support calculus. It does **not** close the outside-`col M` cases (below).

## OPEN (each leaves the class above; priced where a price exists)

- **Label tables of rank `h ≥ 10`, beyond the closed `h = 10` Gram root code.** OPEN: non-Gram rank-8 realisations at `h ≥ 10`; `h = 11` (per-term ≥ 7 except possibly at pair orbit 0 (`N(f) × N(g)`, one split timed out) and at pair orbits not yet run (1, 2, 65–171); runs continue; a 112-port unit must reach cost `≤ 55` to tie); `h ≥ 12` not attempted. Non-dense fitting tables exist at rank 10.
- **Factors outside `col M` with `m ≥ 9`.** `m ≤ 8` is closed. At `m = 9`: (b) one outside factor with `ρ = 8`, (c) a square decoder of a rank-9 realisation (contains the philippeVV co-star families), (d) `m ≥ 10`. **All three remain OPEN**: the frame-module theorem gives a sound SAT model (three positive controls) but the decisive instances timed out under load, and a class-level rank-9 pair test is too weak (136-clique). Swarm results on one explicit rank-9 family, not the general case: #2321, #2385, #2398 (one fixed P112 completion, any number of terms with factors in its 9-dimensional spaces).
- **Bit windows:** 13–14 totals CLOSED (above, RECORDED). Note only: `n ≥ 15` totals are hosting-forbidden; decoders outside the set-decoder model are priced above, not excluded.
- **Puncture windows `p ≥ 46`**, and `p = 45` with `m ≤ 7` (`N`-space nullity > 1). Residue stated in the cards: `m = 8` with a `d ≥ 3` root at `46 ≤ p ≤ 56`; `m ≥ 9` at `p = 46` and wherever the count-relaxed census exceeds its allowance (`p ≥ 50` not computed; `p = 47–49` rest on an uncertified floating-point Q-census); `57 ≤ p ≤ 112` and any-`B` untouched.
- **Batches with `m ≥ 17` terms outside `col M`**, `GL(9)` charts with `k ≥ 3`, `h ≥ 10` joint tables, correlated demands, mixed units.
  Swarm: #2395 (stronger two-call P112 COPY floor for arbitrary cross forms) and #2342 (three-call P112 COPY 192) are cited from their PR statements, not re-derived or compared in scope here; compare with our Theorem Bk.

## Scope and caveats

- The frontier-format hypothesis (one `F2^9` table hosts the whole decoder) is an engineering fact of the word, not proved here; it is exactly what the OPEN `h ≥ 10` item negates.
- Theorem R for P104 is checked for H4's frame (#968's unit; H4 is in the 759 class) and one representative of each of the three invariant classes of disjoint frames (not proven to be single orbits). **Not claimed:** Theorem R or Theorem P for the other P104 units (all 1,260 frames were not finished; the census was run on H4 only), and the rank-9 square decoder (OPEN).
- Theorem P / the headline need the factors in `col M` of a rank-8 realisation; `char 0` is the scope of the co-star consequence (Theorem P and Theorem B are field-independent).
- The pricing consequence of the puncture bounds (break-even `s/f(s) > .1441`, margin under 1%) uses the author's working price model and is RECORDED, not a theorem.
- Word-side overheads (helpers, transport, packing) are out of scope; non-E8 units are out of scope.

## Verification

`bash research/decoder-floors-frontier-format/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python ≥ 3.11, standard library only, one core). Step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json`. On a fresh `git archive` export: **74 PASS (2 in step 0), 0 SKIP, 0 FAIL** with kissat and drat-trim (16 rigidity UNSAT proofs and 10 further drat-trim checks re-derived; about 7 minutes of CPU on a loaded machine), 70 PASS and 4 SKIP without them (about 20 s). `HIT_FULL=1` additionally re-solves three slow clique-hitting instances. `kissat` 4.0.4 and `drat-trim` are optional (`KISSAT=`, `DRAT_TRIM=`); without them the lines that need them print `SKIP`. Overlap check against open and merged PRs (title and body searches; #2294, #2277, #2228, #2062, #2061, #1962, #620, #1097, #1815 read): the credits are in item 1 above and in README §7 (also #717, #1331, #1249; audits #2293 of our CR2/B2 and #2311 of our #2265 premises; the edge-form counterexamples #2334 / #2340 concern an edge-count reading of B2(iii), not the vertex form cited here).
